title: S&P 500 Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE)
revision_note: CAPE divides real price by a 10-year trailing average of real earnings, so it can shift slightly as Shiller revises historical earnings; the site always shows the latest revision.
methodology: CAPE = real (CPI-adjusted) S&P Composite price / the 10-year trailing average of real (CPI-adjusted) as-reported earnings, read directly from Shiller's own CAPE column.

Because the denominator is a 10-year average, CAPE is available for months where Shiller's raw current-quarter earnings figure (see the S&P 500 P/E chart) is not yet known - it lags price by only a few weeks in practice, not a full quarter.
The current, not-yet-completed month is never included: Shiller's own row for it is a placeholder (e.g. a single day's close standing in for the monthly average), not a finished figure.
notes: Built for S9b/S10 (equity-valuation roadmap) alongside dividend yield and earnings yield, all read from the same ie_data.xls download.

Not published on joemirza.com: Shiller's terms are unknown (no statement on the Yale page or shillerdata.com), and the underlying price and earnings columns are S&P's. presentation.publish is false pending an answer from shillerdata.com's maintainer (asked 2026-09-16); scripts/dev.sh builds it locally regardless.

presentation.summary: Monthly S&P 500 cyclically adjusted P/E ratio (CAPE), Shiller/Yale data back to 1881.
